rationale: The agent properly authenticated the user via full name and zip, matched to a single account, and then used read-only tools to locate orders. They correctly identified the Texas-shipped order (#W5565470) and provided the accurate tracking number (907614527588). Before making any changes, the agent stated the intended action (returning all items except the pet bed with refund to PayPal) and requested explicit confirmation, complying with the requirement to confirm before any order-changing write. When the user requested a refund to AMEX and only PayPal was on file, the agent explained the limitation and offered next steps. Upon the user’s request, the agent transferred to a human, which fits policy when the requested action may fall outside tool capabilities. No writes were performed without confirmation, no unsupported tool outputs were stated, and no action was taken on the wrong account. A minor nit is the implication that adding AMEX would enable refunding to that card (not explicitly supported by the provided tools/policy), but since no action was taken and the case was escalated, this does not materially violate the pass criteria.
